item.title: Canadia Impact Fund, Plug and Play APAC to jointly connect Cambodia startups to global stage
item.dc:creator: Duc Dao
item.description: Canadia Impact Fund, an investment fund based in Cambodia, and Plug and Play APAC, a Southeast Asia-focused venture capital, will jointly connect Cambodian start-ups with international networks, expertise and investment opportunities.
item.content:encoded:
Canadia Impact Fund, an investment fund based in Cambodia, and Plug and Play APAC, a Southeast Asia-focused venture capital, will jointly connect Cambodian start-ups with international networks, expertise and investment opportunities.

The two sides have signed signed a memorandum of understanding for the cooperation, at FrancoTech 2026, held at Koh Pich Expo in Cambodia, on the sidelines of the 20th Francophonie Summit. The MoU sets a framework for collaboration to connect Cambodian start-ups with international networks, expertise, and investment opportunities.

From Silicon Valley to Singapore: a global innovation network

Founded in Silicon Valley, Plug and Play is an innovation platform that connects start-ups, corporations, investors and institutions through accelerator programs and corporate innovation activities. With a worldwide presence in more than 30 countries and 60 locations, the APAC operations are based in Singapore, where Plug and Play APAC works with start-ups and stakeholders across the region.

Building the next chapter of Cambodia’s start-up ecosystem

FrancoTech was the moment to formalize a relationship that had already begun. In 2025, the Ministry of Post and Telecommunications (MPTC) brought the Plug and Play accelerator to Cambodia. At the launch of Plug and Play Cambodia, Thierry Tea, Co-Founder of CIFC, met Mike Maceda of Plug and Play APAC and So Visoty, Secretary of State at MPTC in charge of start-up development. Together, they discussed how to work together and build a stronger innovation and tech ecosystem in Cambodia.

In August 2026, Jim Baldy, Senior Investment Associate at CIFC, spoke at the Plug and Play APAC Community Series. His panel, “Bridging the AI Hype and the Founder-Investor Reality”, looked at investment discipline, how founders and investors can stay aligned, and what strategic guidance can add beyond capital.

Prior to the signing of the MOU, Canadia Impact Fund (CIFC) and Plug and Play had already established an investment partnership through their co-investment in Cambodian EdTech startup Bamnang, reflecting their shared commitment to supporting young promising founders.

Thierry Tea said: “In our vision to push the limits and move the lines of innovation investment landscape in Cambodia, we need to build the best talents. In order to succeed in this mission, we have to collaborate with all like minded experts in international tech investments. Entering into a partnership with Plug N Play is the beginning of our learning journey to reach the same level as the best Venture Capital institutions in the world. We are aware that the road ahead is quite long, but we are strongly committed to continue our progress step by step along the growth of the local ecosystem.”

The MoU now turns this strengthened relationship into a more formalized partnership. CIFC and Plug and Play APAC plan to work together on start-up acceleration, mentoring, investor engagement and knowledge sharing, so that Cambodian founders can learn from peers abroad, meet the right people and reach new markets.

Launched in October 2025, Canadia Impact Fund in its first year of operations has invested in tech startups from 4 different countries, including Singapore, Philippines, Cambodia and France covering PropTech, EdTech, Logistics, AI, Software Development and Blockchain solutions.

As Cambodia’s start-up scene grows, Canadia Impact Fund sees international links as a way to help local companies compete beyond the country’s borders.

Canadia Impact Fund backs 2 technology startups Choose & Connect, DOCONCHAIN at FrancoTech

item.title: YTL Power denies Johor’s data center assisted transfer of NVIDIA GPUs to Chinese clients
item.dc:creator: Yimie Yong
item.description: "Various press reports have appeared linking YTL to the current controversy surrounding NVIDIA, some even implying that the YTL data centers have in some way assisted in the transfer of Nvidia GPUs to Chinese customers. These speculative and unsubstantiated reports are completely untrue," the company said in a statement on Friday.
item.content:encoded:
Malaysia-based YTL Power International Bhd has denied allegations that its data centers in Johor were involved in diverting Nvidia chips to Chinese customers.

“Various press reports have appeared linking YTL to the current controversy surrounding NVIDIA, some even implying that the YTL data centers have in some way assisted in the transfer of Nvidia GPUs to Chinese customers. These speculative and unsubstantiated reports are completely untrue,” the company said in a statement on Friday.

YTL Power said YTL Data Centers provides co-location services (space, power, cooling and connectivity) in Johor to multiple global customers, including hyperscalers from the US, under arrangements that are compliant to both local laws and U.S. trade controls.

“YTL has worked closely with the Malaysian Ministry of Investment, Trade and Industry (MITI) on its data centre developments and complied with all applicable reporting and import requirements,” the company said.

YTL Power’s statement came after The New York Times on Thursday reported that YTL Power’s Johor data center was allegedly used by Chinese technology giant Alibaba to remotely access NVIDIA chips through Singapore-based Megaspeed and its Malaysian subsidiary, Speedmatrix.

According to YTL Power, the new interim final rule (Addressing Remote Access to Advanced Semiconductors) issued by the US Department of Commerce Bureau of Industry and Security does not affect YTL’s co-location services as the rule focuses on importers of GPUs and providers of computing services to D:5 customers.

“We remain confident that the demand for co-location data center infrastructure in Malaysia will continue to grow given strong global demand, including from the US,” the company said.

item.title: Fujitsu and Paradigm test AI screening for Japan trials
item.dc:creator: TNGlobal
item.description: Fujitsu, a Japanese cancer center and Paradigm used AI to narrow clinical-trial candidates and reduce records requiring manual review by 89 percent.
item.content:encoded:
Fujitsu Japan, the National Cancer Center Hospital East and US-based Paradigm Health have tested an AI-assisted system for identifying potential participants in clinical trials in Japan.

The partners used a large language model to structure patient information from electronic medical records and linked the resulting data to Paradigm’s clinical trial matching platform, according to a Fujitsu Japan statement on Thursday.

The retrospective verification study covered records from 22,334 patients in the hospital’s respiratory medicine department between June and the end of October. For a simulated trial involving EGFR gene mutations, Fujitsu processed data from 3,027 lung-cancer patients and identified 540 records with the mutation for evaluation against five eligibility criteria.

Paradigm’s platform selected 57 priority candidates and presented clinical evidence supporting those selections. Physicians subsequently reviewed the records and determined that 51 were promising candidates, Fujitsu said.

The study also found that automated overnight processing reduced the number of records requiring manual review by approximately 89 percent. The partners said the approach could help medical staff apply standardized criteria without manually searching dispersed treatment histories, test results and genomic information.

Fujitsu stressed that the output did not determine whether patients were eligible for a real trial. Final eligibility would remain subject to trial requirements, physician review and patient consent.

The work addresses a recruitment challenge in Japan, where increasingly specific genetic and biomarker criteria can make it difficult for clinical staff to identify eligible patients. Fujitsu has also framed the project as part of efforts to reduce “drug loss,” a term used for treatments available overseas that are not developed or approved in Japan.

The company plans to commercialize a service supporting the process from candidate screening through clinical trial enrollment by the end of fiscal 2027. It said the partners intend to promote adoption by medical institutions across Japan.

Paradigm separately reported preliminary findings from the research at the European Society for Medical Oncology Congress in October. The November announcement adds Fujitsu’s detailed workflow, physician-review results and commercialization target.

Fujitsu tackles ‘drug loss’ in Japan through ecosystem to accelerate digitalization of clinical trials

item.title: MetaComp adds about $10M from Tether and Further
item.dc:creator: TNGlobal
item.description: Singapore payments company MetaComp has added about $10 million from Tether and Further, bringing its Pre-A financing to roughly $45 million.
item.content:encoded:
Singapore-headquartered payments company MetaComp has extended its Pre-A+ financing with an investment of approximately $10 million from stablecoin issuer Tether and Abu Dhabi-based Further Asset Management.

The transaction brings MetaComp’s Pre-A and Pre-A+ financing to about $45 million, including a $35 million round completed in March 2026, the company said in a statement on Thursday.

MetaComp said it will use the new capital to strengthen regulatory and compliance capabilities and develop additional payment channels in priority markets. The company is targeting payment corridors linking Asia with the Middle East and Africa, where it serves financial institutions and businesses moving funds across fiat and stablecoin rails.

The Singapore company is licensed by the Monetary Authority of Singapore as a Major Payment Institution. It said its platform connects with more than 60 financial institutions and more than 170 payment service providers, supports 60 currencies across fiat and stablecoins, and processes more than $1 billion in monthly volume.

Those operating figures, including more than 1,000 institutional clients and assets under management exceeding $600 million, were supplied by MetaComp and were stated as accurate as of October 30.

Tether Chief Executive Paolo Ardoino said the investment reflects the company’s focus on regulated stablecoin infrastructure in emerging-market trade corridors. Further, an investment platform focused on financial infrastructure and digital assets, is expected to support MetaComp’s expansion and institutional relationships in the Middle East.

The financing follows MetaComp’s expansion of the StableX Agentic Network, which is designed to route transactions across traditional banking and stablecoin rails. MetaComp said the network has grown to more than 1,000 members reaching more than 100,000 users since its launch in November 2025.

The company also operates compliance tools for transactions initiated by artificial intelligence agents. Its Know-Your-Agent framework governs network admission, while its VisionX system monitors fiat and blockchain activity, according to the announcement.

MetaComp said its March financing was backed by investors including Alibaba, Eastern Bell Capital, Noah, Sky9 Capital and Spark Venture. It did not disclose the valuation or the individual amounts invested by Tether and Further in the extension.

MetaComp scales interoperable payment network to advance cross-border payments in ASEAN

item.title: Malaysia, Philippines Central Banks strengthen cooperation in cross border payment, digitalization
item.dc:creator: TNGlobal Staff
item.description: Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM) and Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP) have on Friday signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) which establishes a framework for collaboration on central banking and financial sector development, including cross-border transactions, financial innovation and digitalization.
item.content:encoded:
Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM) and Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP) have on Friday signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) which establishes a framework for collaboration on central banking and financial sector development, including cross-border transactions, financial innovation and digitalization.

The MoU formalizes the two central banks’ commitment to cooperate on a broad range of areas. These include Islamic finance, cross-border payment linkages, local currency transactions, and financial innovation and digitalization, the banks said in a joint statement.

“This MoU comes at an opportune time as the financial and economic landscape grows increasingly complex. Building on our strong partnership, it enables BNM and BSP to advance shared priorities, learn from each other, pursue new opportunities and navigate emerging challenges together,” BNM Governor Abdul Rasheed Ghaffour said.

BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona, Jr. underscored that the MoU is another big step forward in the long partnership between the BSP and BNM.

“We’ve built a strong foundation, and now the real test is turning it into stronger institutions, better financial infrastructure, and practical programs that genuinely improve life for our people,” he added.

Aside from working together to deliver tangible benefits for both economies, the central banks look forward to translating the framework into meaningful cooperation toward deeper regional financial integration, said the statement.

Four Southeast Asian Central Banks sign MOU to strengthen local currency transactions

item.title: Thailand’s Cho Thavee joins US’ Aether Holdings, Singapore’s ACP on 5.6-hectare AI data centre
item.dc:creator: Duc Dao
item.description: Thailand's Cho Thavee, an industrial company, Aether Holdings, a Nasdaq-listed company, and Advance Capital Partners (ACP), a Singapore-based firm, will jointly build an artificial intelligence (AI) data centre in Khon Kaen Province.
item.content:encoded:
Thailand’s Cho Thavee, an industrial company, Aether Holdings, a Nasdaq-listed company, and Advance Capital Partners (ACP), a Singapore-based firm, will jointly build an artificial intelligence (AI) data centre in Khon Kaen Province.

In a filing with the Stock Exchange of Thailand dated November 19, Cho Thavee said the three sides have signed a binding framework agreement for the move. The three parties will form a joint venture in which Cho Thavee and Aether will each hold 47.5 percent and Advance Capital Partners will hold 5 percent.

The investment value and expected commercial operation date are not available yet, Cho Thavee said.

Cho Thavee will contribute land and infrastructure. Aether will provide technology and expertise in building and running AI infrastructure. Advance Capital Partners will support coordination and funding within terms the parties agree.

The project is initially planned for Cho Thavee’s existing factory site, covering 56,000 square meters. The company said the existing buildings could be converted for use as a data center. The site’s electrical power systems and water reservoir could reduce costs and construction time compared with a new site.

Cho Thavee said the project would take the company beyond its industrial and engineering business into AI infrastructure, using its existing assets to create long-term opportunities.

Thailand data center capacity set to quadruple as hyperscalers drive growth – BMI

item.title: Vietnam proposes 99% Tungsten Oxide criterion for exports, no exports of ore, concentrate
item.dc:creator: Duc Dao
item.description: Vietnam seeks to update technical criteria for exports of various tungsten products, with tungsten oxide required to contain at least 99 percent tungsten trioxide (WO₃).
item.content:encoded:
Vietnam seeks to update technical criteria for exports of various tungsten products, with tungsten oxide required to contain at least 99 percent tungsten trioxide (WO₃).

The requirement is part of a draft circular made by the Ministry of Industry and Trade on mineral export. The draft document does not propose exports of raw tungsten ore or concentrate that has not been refined or smelted.

The draft does not feature a specific date for implementation.

Besides, ammonium paratungstate (APT) must be crystalline, with at least 88.5 percent tungsten expressed as tungsten trioxide.

Ferrotungsten must contain 70-85 percent tungsten by mass and be a true alloy, not a mechanical mixture with ore.

These criteria identify and check products, but do not by themselves allow exports. Ultimately, the Prime Minister decides the list and processing level of tungsten that may be exported from domestic ore.

The draft document recommends that APT, tungsten oxide, and ferrotungsten should feature in the list of eligible for export, but leaving out ore and concentrate. It clarified that Vietnam already has an industrial processing chain with Masan High-Tech Materials as a key company. Besides, concentrate is used as feedstock for further processing at home.

The ministry also pointed out that tungsten resources are about 309.41 thousand tons of tungsten trioxide, concentrated in Thai Nguyen province. Further occurrences are recorded in Tuyen Quang, Thanh Hoa, Quang Ngai, and Lam Dong provinces.

Masan High-Tech Materials, under Vietnamese conglomerate Masan, reported its January-September 2026 post-tax profit of VND4.35 trillion dong ($168 million). The figure is better than a loss of VND211 billion in the same period of 2025.

On production, Masan High-Tech Materials said the current output is 6,000 tons and the target is 8,000 tons in 2027. Besides, orders for 2027 nearly fill planned capacity. It has signed a concentrate-supply cooperation with South Korea’s GB Innovation.

Vietnam proposes 99% purity standard for rare earth exports

item.title: 65 Equity Partners surpasses $2B investment milestone with Koenigsegg deal
item.dc:creator: TNGlobal Staff
item.description: Singapore-based investment firm 65 Equity Partners has deployed more than $2 billion across 19 investments globally since its establishment five years ago, marking a milestone in its expansion as it backs Swedish hypercar manufacturer Koenigsegg Automotive.
item.content:encoded:
Singapore-based investment firm 65 Equity Partners has deployed more than $2 billion across 19 investments globally since its establishment five years ago, marking a milestone in its expansion as it backs Swedish hypercar manufacturer Koenigsegg Automotive.

The firm said in a statement that it continues to expand its presence in Europe with an investment in Koenigsegg Automotive.

Koenigsegg is the fourth European investment completed by 65 Equity Partners over the past 24 months, reflecting the breadth of opportunities across the region and growing demand from successful entrepreneurs and family-owned businesses for long-term minority capital to support their growth ambitions.

65 Equity Partners’ investment in Koenigsegg will provide new capital to support the company’s next phase of growth, continued technology development and preparations ahead of a potential future listing.

Founded in 1994 by Christian von Koenigsegg, the company has established itself as one of the world’s hypercar manufacturers, combining pioneering engineering and technological innovation with a globally recognized luxury brand.

Koenigsegg has delivered average annual revenue growth of 80 percent in recent years since 2022 and an order backlog extending more than three years.

Christian von Koenigsegg will remain the majority shareholder and continue to lead the business.

The Koenigsegg transaction follows 65 Equity Partners’ recent investment in Theop, an independent real estate project management consultancy, operating across several European markets, including France, Spain, Belgium and Italy.

65 Equity Partners’ partnership with Theop’s founders, Julien Palengat and Sébastien Alphand, will support the next phase of the company’s development, including expansion into new geographies and adjacent asset classes, organic growth and merger and acquisition (M&A), and further investment in digitalization and AI.

These investments build on two European transactions completed in 2025. In the United Kingdom, 65 Equity Partners invested in Kee Safety, a global safety systems and solutions firm.

In Switzerland, 65 Equity Partners partnered with the Braglia family, providing the first institutional capital to support the merger of HAS and Cerbios, creating an international pharmaceutical development and manufacturing group and a strong platform to accelerate further growth.

Together, the four investments reflect 65 Equity Partners’ approach to minority investing, partnering with successful businesses across a range of sectors to provide capital and strategic support for ambitious growth plans while enabling existing shareholders to retain control.

65 Equity Partner said the market for minority investments is benefiting from a structural shift, as more successful founders and family shareholders seek external capital to finance growth, acquisitions and international expansion without ceding control of their businesses.

Research published by 65 Equity Partners in partnership with INSEAD, covering more than 19,000 businesses across nine countries, highlights the scale of this opportunity.

The research found that 26 percent of family businesses expect to seek outside investment over the next three to five years, while just 3 percent anticipate an outright sale.

“Reaching $2 billion of investment globally is an important milestone for 65 Equity Partners and reflects the progress we have made since launching five years ago,

“Europe is an increasingly important part of our business and our four recent investments across a range of sectors demonstrate the breadth of the European investment opportunity and our ability to partner with exceptional entrepreneurs and businesses,” said Alex Stirling, Partner and Co-Head of Europe at 65 Equity Partners.

Pascal Heberling, Partner and Co-Head of Europe at 65 Equity Partners, said they are seeing a fundamental shift in how successful entrepreneurs and families think about external capital.

“Increasingly, they want to bring in a partner who can help them accelerate growth, expand internationally and strengthen their businesses, without giving up control or compromising the entrepreneurial culture that has made them successful,

“Our research with INSEAD highlights the scale of this opportunity, with more than a quarter of family businesses expecting to seek external investment over the next three to five years, but very few contemplating an outright sale. We believe this creates a significant opportunity for our flexible, long-term approach to minority investing，” he added.

StraitsX, OCBC, Standard Chartered explore interoperability between tokenized deposits networks

item.title: StraitsX, OCBC, Standard Chartered explore interoperability between tokenized deposits networks
item.dc:creator: TNGlobal Staff
item.description: StraitsX, OCBC and Standard Chartered have completed a proof of concept (POC) exploring how tokenized deposits issued by different banks can be used for payments between financial institutions.
item.content:encoded:
StraitsX, OCBC and Standard Chartered have completed a proof of concept (POC) exploring how tokenized deposits issued by different banks can be used for payments between financial institutions.

The parties developed and tested the model through a POC under the Monetary Authority of Singapore’s (MAS) BLOOM initiative, addressing a growing interoperability challenge as banks develop their own tokenized deposit ecosystems, the trio said in a statement on Thursday.

As tokenized deposits represent claims against their issuing banks only, they cannot be seamlessly transferred across different banks’ tokenized deposit ecosystems, which may operate on different platforms and standards.

The POC demonstrated how StraitsX’s shared settlement infrastructure could coordinate payments to achieve end-to-end settlement across OCBC’s and Standard Chartered’s tokenized deposit ecosystems, including payment initiation, compliance screening, liquidity checks, settlement and confirmation.

The participants also observed that the shared model reduced the need for bilateral prefunding arrangements, demonstrating the potential for more efficient liquidity management compared with conventional models. The POC follows frameworks established under BLOOM.

It is noted that many traditional interbank USD payment flows operate within fixed settlement windows and are unavailable outside business hours.

Tokenized deposits on distributed ledgers can settle in near real-time and outside conventional banking hours. To realize that potential across institutions, however, different banks’ tokenized deposit ecosystems need to be able to work together.

Through the controlled POC, StraitsX, OCBC and Standard Chartered tested payment flows using tokenized deposits from both participating banks.

StraitsX coordinated payment instructions and transaction information between the institutions, supported screening coordination and settlement after applicable compliance, eligibility and liquidity checks.

The POC successfully completed USD payment flows outside conventional banking cut-off windows, demonstrating how interoperable tokenized deposit infrastructure could enable always-on value movement across participating banks’ separate tokenized deposit ecosystems within minutes, including the necessary compliance, liquidity and settlement processes.

It showed how tokenized deposits from different issuers could be treated as equivalent within a shared interoperability framework, providing an early indication of how a shared interoperability model could support faster, always-on institutional payments while reducing the need for bilateral prefunding arrangements.

As more financial institutions explore tokenized forms of money, further development will require assessment of the legal, regulatory, operational and commercial arrangements needed for broader implementation, including settlement finality, liquidity management, participant responsibilities and financial-crime controls.

“Tokenized deposits have the potential to enable near-instant and programmable money movement, but their broader utility will depend on how effectively different banking ecosystems can connect,” said Tianwei Liu, Chief Executive Officer and Co-Founder of StraitsX.

“Together with OCBC and Standard Chartered, we are exploring how shared settlement infrastructure can support that interoperability while reducing the need for bilateral arrangements and prefunded liquidity between individual participants,” he added.

Meanwhile, Carmen Chan, Deputy Head, Global Transaction Banking, OCBC. said tokenized deposits can bring the trust of commercial bank money into an increasingly digital and always-on economy.

“Their full potential, however, will depend on interoperability across banking ecosystems,

“Through MAS’ BLOOM initiative, we are exploring with industry partners how shared infrastructure could enable seamless value movement across banks, while preserving the regulatory safeguards, integrity of bank deposits and trusted banking relationships that underpin the financial system,” she said.

She also said this collaboration is an important step towards understanding how interoperable tokenized deposits could support the future of institutional payments.

Ankur Kanwar, Head of Transaction Banking & Cash Management, Singapore & ASEAN, Global Head of Payment and Treasury Solutions, Standard Chartered, said for digital assets to scale, the industry needs to move beyond individual solutions towards a more connected and interoperable financial ecosystem.

“That requires collaboration across institutions to build the trust, credibility and connectivity needed for broader adoption. Standard Chartered’s approach is centered on helping orchestrate that ecosystem, connecting capabilities and participants so that tokenized assets and different forms of money can work together more effectively,

“Collaborations like this are an important part of turning that ambition into practical, scalable infrastructure,” he added.

NETS, Ant International deepen partnership to expand Singapore’s digital payments ecosystem

item.title: Yeahka and Mastercard demonstrate agent-pay purchase in Singapore
item.dc:creator: TNGlobal
item.description: Yeahka and Mastercard demonstrated an AI-assisted bubble-tea purchase that moved from product discovery to authorized payment in one conversation.
item.content:encoded:
Hong Kong-listed payment technology company Yeahka and Mastercard have demonstrated an artificial intelligence-assisted purchase that moved from product discovery to payment within a single conversation at the Singapore FinTech Festival.

The demonstration used a bubble-tea order to show how an AI agent could search nearby merchants, retrieve product information, build an order and initiate payment after the consumer confirmed the transaction. The companies also signed a cooperation agreement to explore further agent-driven commerce applications.

Under the setup described in Yeahka’s November 19 announcement, Mastercard’s app served as the consumer interface. It integrated an AI-agent payment service from YeahPay, Yeahka’s international payments brand, while Yeahka subsidiary Fushi Tech supplied merchant and product information.

A consumer could ask the agent to find a nearby bubble-tea shop and order a drink. The system then used Fushi Tech’s merchant services to identify stores and display products, prices, sizes and toppings. After the consumer selected an item and confirmed the order, the agent initiated the transaction through YeahPay. The payment remained subject to user authorization and security checks.

The example was a festival demonstration rather than evidence of a broad commercial rollout. Yeahka said the companies intend to explore integrations that connect product discovery, order creation and payment, but it did not disclose a launch timetable, merchant coverage or transaction volume for the arrangement.

The Singapore demonstration gives the collaboration a direct Asia-Pacific use case as payment networks and regional fintech companies test how software agents can act on verified consumer instructions. Mastercard and Ant International separately announced a live consumer transaction and a machine-payment pilot in Singapore this week, while Visa has expanded an Asia-Pacific program intended to prepare acquirers, payment providers and merchants for agent-initiated transactions.

Agent-led payments require controls that conventional online checkout flows do not always expose directly. A provider must verify the software agent, confirm that the user authorized it to act and ensure that an instruction remains within the user’s permissions. YeahPay said it is exploring payment protocols, identity verification and delegated-authorization mechanisms for those requirements.

Yeahka said developers can access YeahPay’s AI-agent payment software development kit and technical documentation from its website. The company is listed in Hong Kong under stock code 9923 and operates payment and merchant technology businesses through YeahPay and Fushi Tech.

YeahPay targets the trust gap holding back autonomous AI shopping
